sentences.text: The operating concept is governed as a controlled baseline for safe, reliable, and compliant offshore wind farm operations.
The asset operator assigns an accountable owner to maintain the document and coordinate its approval.
Changes to operating assumptions, responsibilities, interfaces, or decision authority require documented impact assessment before approval.
The assessment considers effects on personnel safety, marine coordination, electrical safety, availability, cybersecurity, and regulatory obligations.
The approved concept is consistent with applicable permits, grid requirements, safety cases, and company management systems.
The Shore Control Room applies the approved operating concept during routine operations and abnormal conditions.
The Control Engineer reviews control-room practices and confirms that operational procedures remain consistent with the concept.
The Duty Planner checks that maintenance priorities, resource plans, and operational constraints are reflected in planned work.
The Marine Coordinator reviews vessel coordination arrangements and verifies that marine responsibilities are understood.
The HSE Officer evaluates safety controls, emergency arrangements, and lessons from reported events.
The SCADA Engineer reviews monitoring and control assumptions that affect operational decisions.
The Cybersecurity Analyst assesses changes that could affect access, communications, or the integrity of operational records.
The Field Supervisor confirms that field execution practices and escalation routes are workable for offshore personnel.
The Substation Operator reviews responsibilities and coordination arrangements for substation activities.
Assurance evidence includes approved procedures, competence records, maintenance records, risk assessments, audit findings, and event investigations.
Evidence is retained in controlled repositories with access permissions, revision history, and defined retention periods.
Reviews distinguish verified evidence from assumptions, unresolved actions, and proposals that have not yet been approved.
Nonconformances and operational lessons are assigned to an accountable owner with a due date and closure evidence.
The document owner schedules periodic review and initiates an additional review after material operational, technical, or regulatory change.
Review findings are assessed for their effect on existing procedures, training, interfaces, and resource requirements.
Proposed revisions are checked by affected operational and technical representatives before submission to the designated approver.
The approver confirms that comments are resolved or explicitly accepted before the revised baseline is released.
Released revisions identify the change, rationale, approval, effective date, and superseded baseline.
Personnel affected by a revision receive appropriate communication or training before the change takes effect.
Unapproved local variations are not treated as changes to the operating concept and are escalated through established governance channels.
The operator periodically evaluates whether assurance arrangements provide sufficient evidence that the concept remains effective.
